methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series C → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.7x) to $1.0B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Waabi, a Series C-stage autonomous transportation company founded by Raquel Urtasun, operates within a fragmented frontier-tech Transportation sector. The comparable universe consists of seven private peers including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Slate Auto, and ZeroAvia, with no public comparables available.

Stage-progression methodology proves applicable, using Waabi's $1.0B total raised as a valuation proxy. Applying a typical Series C-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 1.7x yields an implied valuation of $1.7B. Peer-median triangulation does not apply: while three same-sector peers exist in Transportation, none satisfy the narrow filtering criteria of matching stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier simultaneously. A sector-wide median would lack sufficient homogeneity to be reliable.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $1.4B (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $1.7B. This range is derived from a single methodological input, which represents a material constraint on confidence. Key uncertainties include the absence of directly comparable Series C Transportation benchmarks and reliance on stage-progression mechanics rather than revenue or market-derived multiples. Any valuation within this band should be stress-tested against capital deployment efficiency and stage-appropriate metrics from the broader frontier-tech ecosystem.
